maine.title: More addresses found and corrected year over year
maine.obs: Return mail New results rose 22.1% (6,255 → 7,635) and Improved rose 26.1% (836 → 1,054), Jan–Jun 2024 vs 2025.
maine.so: Improved addresses grew slightly faster, lifting the improved share from 11.8% to 12.1% of corrected accounts.
maine.rec: Use the New and Improved volumes to size automation: improved-only automation is the low-risk first step.

maine.title: Q3 value is driven by stronger patient payment performance
maine.obs: Patient payments rose 32.4% year over year (Jul–Sep: $45.2M → $59.8M) and the collection rate improved 3.18 points (6.58% → 9.76%).
maine.so: Payment growth outpaced inventory growth, so the lift reflects better collection effectiveness, not just more volume.
maine.rec: Keep segmentation-based strategies in place and track the collection rate monthly to confirm the gain holds through Q4.

maine.title: ROI rests almost entirely on one lever
maine.obs: Recovery lift is 95.8% of Q3 quantified benefit ($464,737 of $485,089).
maine.so: If the collection rate softens, ROI drops sharply. Automation and statement savings are mostly sitting in “additional value,” not the ROI.
maine.rec: Quantify return mail, bankruptcy and deceased automation so the ROI has a second, steadier leg before renewal.

maine.title: Workbook “% change” formulas understate growth
maine.obs: The Cash Impact change formulas divide by the current period, so the Q3 deck shows patient payments +24.4%. Measured against the prior year it is +32.4%.
maine.so: The client-facing number is conservative but inconsistent with how a CFO would calculate growth.
maine.rec: Standardize the template to (current − prior) ÷ prior, or label the metric clearly.

maine.title: Low income does not mean low likelihood to pay
maine.obs: 44.6% of patients are at or below 200% FPL, yet 73.6% score high propensity to pay.
maine.so: A policy that writes off on FPL alone would forgo payments from patients who are likely to pay.
maine.rec: Use segment/propensity alongside FPL in the presumptive charity policy.

maine.title: Front-end address correction is reducing returned mail
maine.obs: 27.2% of PIV transactions returned a new or improved address, and return mail volume fell 94% (17,917 → 1,140).
maine.so: Cleaner addresses at registration mean fewer returned statements and less rework downstream.
maine.rec: Present PIV and Return Mail together as one address-quality story.

maine.title: Fewer but larger bankruptcy balances
maine.obs: Bankruptcy results rose 20% (92 → 110) while impacted dollars rose 161% ($38K → $100K); the average balance more than doubled ($415 → $906).
maine.so: Each missed bankruptcy now carries more compliance and write-off exposure.
maine.rec: Confirm bankruptcy holds are automated; the workbook sizes manual handling at 18.3 hours this quarter.

maine.title: Deceased hits are down sharply
maine.obs: Deceased results fell 61% (104 → 41) year over year.
maine.so: Lower volume reduces manual research, but a drop this large can also reflect a change in what is being scrubbed.
maine.rec: Confirm the deceased scrub population did not change before presenting this as an improvement.

maine.title: Return mail is a ready automation candidate
maine.obs: 77.5% of return mail searches found a new, improved or equal address, and updated accounts produced $20,352 in payments.
maine.so: Most returned mail can be corrected automatically; manual handling costs about 901.5 hours (1.73 FTE) per quarter.
maine.rec: Propose automating improved and new address updates, starting with improved only if the client prefers.

maine.title: Charity qualified volume fell by half
maine.obs: Qualified accounts fell 51% (308,006 → 150,396) and qualified balance fell 55% ($167.3M → $74.9M).
maine.so: A drop this large usually means a policy, timing or filter change rather than a change in patient need.
maine.rec: Review with the client whether presumptive charity criteria or timing changed during 2025.

maine.title: Charity counts differ between the deck and workbook
maine.obs: The Q3 deck shows 308,006 accounts for Jul–Sep 2024; the workbook shows 155,730 for all of Jan–Jun 2024.
maine.so: Comparing the two could mislead the client.
maine.rec: Confirm both use the same Tableau report view before the next review.

maine.title: Segments 1–2 carry the payments
maine.obs: Segments 1–2 are 53% of volume but 74% of payments; segments 4–5 are 22% of volume and about 10% of payments.
maine.so: Effort spent on segments 4–5 returns little cash.
maine.rec: Shift dialer and statement effort toward segments 1–3 and consider earlier charity screening or offload for segments 4–5.

washu.title: Return mail corrections dropped sharply in 2024
washu.obs: New results fell 66.8% (6,255 → 2,076) and Improved fell 70.5% (836 → 247), Jan–Jun 2023 vs 2024.
washu.so: Either far less mail is being returned or fewer returned accounts are being sent through the scrub.
washu.rec: Confirm all returned mail is routed to the scrub, and fill in the Jan–Jun 2025 row before the next review.

washu.title: Balances grew faster than payments
washu.obs: Outstanding patient balance rose 16.1% while patient payments rose 3.0%, so the collection rate fell 2.05 points (18.16% → 16.11%).
washu.so: The ROI uses patient-payment lift ($2.07M) because recovery-rate lift was negative. A CFO may challenge that.
washu.rec: Lead with the inventory explanation below and present a conservative ROI alongside the full ROI.

washu.title: Inventory shifted to higher-balance accounts
washu.obs: Accounts placed fell 36.7% (1.39M → 881K) while dollars placed were flat (+1.1%), so the average placed balance rose 60% ($129 → $206).
washu.so: Higher-balance self-pay is harder to collect, which explains much of the collection-rate decline.
washu.rec: Frame the period as “holding payments steady on a harder inventory” and review segment strategy for high balances.

washu.title: Cash impact is 64% of the ROI
washu.obs: Cash impact is 64.2% of quantified benefit; Medicaid is 18.9% and return mail 10.1%. Excluding cash impact, ROI is 6.2 : 1 instead of 17.2 : 1.
washu.so: The headline ROI is sensitive to how cash impact is calculated.
washu.rec: Have the 6.2 : 1 conservative figure ready for renewal conversations.

washu.title: Medicaid payments fell despite a better hit rate
washu.obs: Medicaid payments fell 57% (Jan–Jun: $1.42M → $609K) while the hit rate rose (8.0% → 10.2%).
washu.so: Fewer dollars with a higher hit rate points to fewer or lower-balance accounts being scrubbed, or timely-filing loss.
washu.rec: Check scrub scope (true self-pay, Medicare no secondary) and timely-filing windows; consider expanding to neighboring states if enrolled.

washu.title: Presumptive charity is growing
washu.obs: Qualified accounts rose 29% (23,421 → 30,214) and qualified balance rose 27% ($11.3M → $14.3M).
washu.so: More patients are being identified for assistance before bad debt, which supports compliance and reduces wasted collection effort.
washu.rec: Check segment overlap so likely payers (segments 1–3) are not written off on FPL alone.

washu.title: Improved-address rate is slipping
washu.obs: PIV improved addresses fell from 4.79% to 3.55% of volume (2023 → 2025) while new-address rate held near 17%.
washu.so: Fewer corrections at registration can push more work to return mail later.
washu.rec: Review PIV/PFC configuration with the client to confirm all patients are being sent through.

washu.title: Bankruptcy volume up 19%
washu.obs: Bankruptcy results rose 19% (6,975 → 8,274) with about $1.31M in impacted balance.
washu.so: More accounts are being correctly removed from active collection.
washu.rec: Confirm adjustments are automated; manual handling is sized at $15,169 for the period.

washu.title: Bankruptcy dollars jump in 2024
washu.obs: Average bankruptcy balance went from $14 (2023) to $181 (2024).
washu.so: A 13× jump is more likely a report filter change than real behavior.
washu.rec: Re-pull Jan–Jun 2023 bankruptcy dollars before showing the 3-year trend.

washu.title: Deceased results down 35%
washu.obs: Deceased results fell 35% (2,259 → 1,462) year over year.
washu.so: Lower volume reduces sensitive manual work.

washu.title: Both agencies trail the benchmark
washu.obs: Over 24 months, Agency A recovers at 41% of benchmark (3.42% vs 8.27%) and Agency B at 74% (6.13%).
washu.so: Placements to Agency A are recovering well below what comparable inventory achieves elsewhere.
washu.rec: Review placement allocation and consider shifting inventory toward the stronger agency.

washu.title: Return mail 2025 New/Improved is blank
washu.obs: The workbook Jan–Jun 2025 New/Improved row is empty.
washu.so: Year-over-year return mail improvement cannot be shown.
washu.rec: Fill from the Return Mail dashboard before the next review.
